specs.cpu: AMD Ryzen AI 9 HX 370 (12-core: 4 Zen5 + 8 Zen5c)
specs.gpu: NVIDIA GeForce RTX 5080 Laptop 16GB (severely TGP-capped in 1.5kg chassis, ~100-110W)

battery.notes: 73Wh with the hungriest GPU of the line; -1h vs anchor per SHARED-zephyrus-g14.md. ~1h gaming.

price.notes: NOT verified on Best Buy CA today (ROG_LIST.md: seen historically on asus.com/ca configurator, est. $5,500-6,000). Midpoint estimate; treat as indicative only. A CA 5080 G14 tier may not be in current stock — verify before purchase.

reviews.quote: With the RTX 5070 Ti and RTX 5080 options the new ROG Zephyrus G14 is currently pretty unrivaled. Very high-quality and compact aluminum case, brilliant OLED display at 120 Hz with G-Sync, excellent speakers, great input devices. Cons: soldered-on RAM, PWM flickering, limited maximum HDR brightness, loud fans. (NBC review of the GA403WW RTX 5080 config, "top rated" award.)

professional.note: No pro review retrieved for this tier (hard-stop, disclosed). Anchored on GA403 line via SHARED-zephyrus-g14.md.

praises: 16GB VRAM RTX 5080 in a 1.5kg laptop is unmatched for portable AI/ML work (local LLMs) in the G14 line
Class-leading 3K OLED 120Hz panel and premium aluminum chassis shared across the line
Enough GPU headroom that 1080p/1440p gaming is effortless even with the TGP cap
Still USB-C chargeable and genuinely portable unlike 5080-equipped 16-18" bricks
complaints: The 5080 is severely power-limited (~100-110W vs 150W+ rated) — buyers pay 5080 money for well-below-5080 performance; a thicker 5070 Ti laptop often matches it
Est. ~$5,500-6,000 CAD puts it against full-size 5080/5090 machines — extreme thin-and-light tax
Hot under load and loud in Turbo; the 1.5kg chassis cannot dissipate a 5080
Soldered RAM and single M.2 at this price; no upgrade path
Canadian availability unconfirmed today — may only be orderable via ASUS store with long lead times

design_philosophy: The theoretical ceiling of ASUS's thin-and-light gaming bet: cram a 16GB RTX 5080 into the same 1.5kg aluminum OLED chassis, accepting heavy TGP capping and thermal compromise to keep the portability that defines the line. It exists for buyers who absolutely need discrete-GPU VRAM on the road; value-wise the chassis physics work against it.
